title: Nourishing Vietnamese Flax Pho
description: A silky, glassy-jelly pho with flax eggs and fresh leaf wraps, perfect for a brunch-time Vietnamese twist.

ingredients.name: vegetable stock with lemongrass ginger onion garlic star anise

instructions: Combine 1 cup flax seeds with 3 cups water in a saucepan and bring to a boil, stirring constantly until the mixture thickens into a gelled egg-like consistency.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and let the flax egg mixture steam for 8 minutes to fully set.
In a separate pot, bring the 8 cups vegetable stock with lemongrass ginger onion garlic star anise to a simmer and strain to remove solids.
Stir in 2 tsp agar-agar powder until fully dissolved, then add 1 cup coconut milk, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tsp black pepper, and simmer for 5 minutes to develop a glassy broth.
While the broth thickens, cut 200 g tofu into 1/2-inch cubes and set aside.
Place the tofu cubes into the broth and simmer gently for 3 minutes to absorb flavors.
Separate 4 rice paper sheets, soak each briefly in warm water until pliable, then lay flat on a clean surface.
Spread a thin layer of tofu and spoonfuls of bean sprouts, julienned carrot, and shiitake mushrooms onto each sheet, then fold to form small leaf-wrap rolls.
Steam the rolled sheets in a steamer basket over boiling water for 4 minutes until translucent and slightly chewy.
Serve the steamed leaf wraps alongside the sugary-jelly pho broth, garnished with fresh basil, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime.
